description.narrative: Based on a request from the Ministry of Environmental Protection in Serbia the second phase of a project reducing industrial emissions and strengthening Serbia´s EU accession process with a focus on Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control (IPPC) and the Industrial Emissions Direcive (IED). The project gives special attention to the food sector performance. Activities will aim at supporting the preparation of the negotiation position of Chapter 27, the EU environmental policy chapter. The project is implemented by the Cleaner Production Centre in Serbia (CPCS) at Belgrade University and in cooperation with the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

Mot bakgrund av en förfrågan från det serbiska miljöministeriet inleddes andra fasen av ett projekt för att minska industrins utsläpp och stärka Serbiens tillnärmning till EU och genomförandet av Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control (IPPC) samt Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) med ett särskilt fokus på matindustrin. Projektet bidrar med underlag för att förbereda Serbiens förhandlingsposition av Kapitel 27, EU:s miljölagstiftning. Projektet genomförs av Cleaner Production Centre Serbia (CPCS) vid Belgrad Universitet och i samarbete med Miljöministeriet.

The general objective is to support the Serbian authorities and a selection of companies (operators) in the food production chain in the implementation of the EU Industrial Emission Directive (IED), in order to foster technological improvement and reduce the impact on the environment (i.e air, water, energy efficiency). Specific components are: 1) Supporting the preparation of Negotiation Position for Chapter 27. Sweden and Serbia cooperate on EU environmental reform in Serbia, the environmental and climate Chapter 27. Under the first component support prepared the legislative framework in Serbia implementing the EU Industrial Emission Directive (IED). 2) Technical support to companies and competent authorities involved in the process of issuance and control of integrated permits for installations in the food sector. 3) Promotion of technological improvement in the food production chain. Promoting economic integration with the EU and development of market economy and develop innovative market opportunities. 4) Awareness and capacity building through education and events. The project is implemented by the Cleaner Production Center at the Faculty of Technology and Metallurgy (Belgrade University), in cooperation with the Serbian Ministry of Environmental Protection.

The overall assessment is that the contribution has well achieved the objectives of the intervention and created short and long term results. The contribution has strengthened the capacity of the Government and Ministry of Environmental protection on EU environmental industrial policy reform, and contributed to building capacity at local level, in companies and within the educational structure at the University of Belgrade. The intervention has also contributed in preparing the readiness for permitting procedures and investments in clean technologies. On the four components: 1) Supporting the preparation of Negotiation Position for Chapter 27 Sweden and Serbia cooperate on strengthening EU environmental reform in Serbia, including the EU legislative package on environment and climate, Chapter 27. Under the first component, support has been given to strengthen to the legislative framework in Serbia, implementing the EU Industrial Emission Directive (IED). The achieved results include: - Analysis and preparation of legislation and a Directive Specific Implementation Plan (DSIP) has been completed. This was an important contribution when Serbia's finalised its Negotiating Position on Chapter 27. The Negotiating position was submitted to the EU Commission in 2020. 2) Technical support to companies and competent authorities involved in the process of issuance and control of integrated permits for installations in the food sector. The achieved results include: - A number of municipalities and companies have been supported in permitting processes and 10 draft permits have been prepared, including a template of integrated permits for installations in food sector and training of almost 50 inspectors. - A number of permits for farms prepared, contributing to reduced environmental impact. - Best Available Technology assessments have been made, an important basis for future investments in green industry. 3) Promotion of technological improvement in the food production chain. Promoting economic integration with the EU and development of market economy and develop innovative market opportunities. The achieved results include: - Analysis and support to the preparation of several environmental investment projects in the food production chain. 4) Awareness and capacity building through education and events The achieved results include: - More than 600 participants trained at workshops. - Several trainings of inspection to improve environmental performance in businesses. - More than 130 students involved in education and trainings, including high school competitions. - Broad media activities communicating advantages with EU environmental standards in industry.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
